frameforge_implications: Design inference: retain source-level evidence and version constraints; do not present a current documentation snapshot as a complete dated release history.
limitations: [uncertain] Exact introduction dates inside the requested window for undated current features, including packages and reviews, were not independently established. Version thresholds are documented, not guessed. No pre-window dated source was needed; the December 2025 announcement supplies the explicitly labeled historical 1.x baseline. Search summaries were discovery aids only; unsupported duplicate-workflow guarantees and the incorrect trigger-restart retry summary were excluded.

observed_facts: A workflow is a connected collection of nodes. Creation can target a personal space or a project; creating inside a project puts the workflow there. Projects group workflows and credentials and assign per-project roles.

A workflow has an ID usable in its URL and sub-workflow calls. Saved workflow versions are different from execution instances. History creates versions on save, restore and source-control pull; changing workflow settings does not create a new version.

The current save/publish documentation says autosave creates draft changes and production executes the specifically published version. Restoring history can change the working version without changing production. Clone to new workflow creates a separate workflow, not an ongoing shared link.
Execution lists are available at workflow, project and overview scope. Parent and sub-workflow execution views link to one another. Deleting a workflow deletes its execution history.

Historical baseline explicitly reported by the December 8, 2025 announcement: saving an activated workflow in 1.x immediately changed production. That behavior must not be carried into the current draft/publish model.

Current named-version retention and full history are plan-dependent. The history page documents last-24-hour access for all users, five days on Cloud Pro, and full history on Enterprise; named versions are protected from automatic pruning on eligible plans.
frameforge_implications: Design inference: model project ID, reusable definition ID, immutable definition revision, production instance ID, node-run ID and output artifact ID separately. Keep selected production and run context while moving between graph, inspector, history and output review.
Design inference: use explicit snapshot/copy/live-reference labels; preserve source lineage when deriving a production from a reusable definition.
limitations: n8n is not a video sequence or asset-management model. Persistent selection across navigation is not established by these documentation pages. A saved graph revision does not freeze credentials, variables, workflow settings or dependent sub-workflows.

observed_facts: Nodes start workflows, retrieve/send data, process data or implement control logic. Trigger and action operations are distinct. Execute Sub-workflow accepts named typed input fields or a JSON example, or accepts all data without a declared required-input schema; optional conversion can attempt to match requested types.

Double-clicking a node exposes input/output with Schema, Table and JSON views. Schema summarizes only the first item; Table and JSON expose the dataset. Saved execution logs allow inspection of data passing through nodes, subject to saving, redaction and access rules.

Execute step is a manual partial execution of the selected node and preceding nodes needed for its inputs. It requires a connected trigger. Large branched execution payloads can exceed partial-execution message limits. Pinning substitutes stored node output in manual runs; production ignores pinned data.

Dirty nodes identify stale output after parameter, graph or pinned-data changes; a yellow triangle and changed border replace the prior success indication, with a tooltip in the output pane. Rerunning the affected node or a following step can clear dirty status.

Official current retry documentation says a failed retry resumes saved execution state, retaining completed-node results. The failed node receives its saved input and reprocesses every item, including items it completed before failure. Retrying a failed Execute Sub-workflow node restarts that entire child workflow. Each retry creates a new execution.

Retry with original workflow uses the original graph; Retry with currently saved workflow applies changes only to nodes that have not completed. Both reload credentials at retry time. Successful executions cannot use failed-execution retry. Debug in editor or Copy to editor instead loads old data into the current graph and pins the first node, which can repeat downstream external actions.

Node settings expose Retry On Fail and On Error choices: stop workflow, continue, or continue using error output. Workflow settings control saving failed/successful/manual runs and per-node progress, and expose an execution timeout. The command bar documents stopping executions. History filters include Failed, Running, Success and Waiting.
frameforge_implications: Design inference: expose role, declared inputs, resolved inputs, output artifacts, dependency revision, status, errors and original execution lineage in one node inspector. Distinguish pinned test data, retained successful evidence and invalidated output.

Design inference: rerun UI should preview the exact restart boundary and external side effects. Give uploads and other irreversible steps idempotency/read-back protection; restarting a failed multi-item node is not guaranteed exactly-once delivery.

Design inference: make cancellation, pause/wait, retry-original, retry-with-edits and replay-from-source separate operations. Retain artifact evidence independently of a deleted graph when audit obligations require it.
limitations: No execution was run. Documentation does not establish transactional rollback of external effects on cancellation. Retry requires retained execution data; save settings, deletion and retention can remove that capability. General data items should not be described as universally strongly typed merely because sub-workflow inputs can declare types. Execution redaction and end-user credential visibility can deliberately hide node data.

observed_facts: Not applicable as a native footage marketplace or rights-clearance product. The investigated official n8n documentation describes workflow automation and data transfer, not a built-in license grant for discovered footage.

Workflow JSON can carry credential names/IDs and raw HTTP authentication headers imported from cURL; official documentation warns to remove or anonymize sensitive information before sharing. This is workflow portability evidence, not proof of rights to the media a workflow retrieves.
frameforge_implications: Design inference: a retrieval node should emit a separate provenance record containing source/provider asset ID, canonical source URL, retrieval time, license terms evidence, attribution and file identity/hash. Workflow success must not stand in for reuse permission.
Design inference: separate public availability, authentic origin and legal reuse authorization; make a rights gate an explicit dependency of delivery.
limitations: No footage was searched, downloaded or licensed. No provider-specific attribution, derivative or redistribution permission is inferred from n8n connectivity. Rights evidence must come from the actual footage provider and applicable license.

observed_facts: The workflow canvas composes connected nodes. Node detail views inspect input/output and parameters; data inspection supports Schema, Table and JSON. Manual execution flow is visible in the Editor, while production execution evidence is inspected through Executions rather than animated in the Editor.

Workflow history provides a version list and a preview canvas. Open version in new tab supports comparison; restore, clone and download are separate actions. Parent/child execution links permit navigation through reusable sub-workflow runs.

Keyboard shortcuts document workflow opening, graph pan and zoom-to-fit, directional node selection, Enter to open the selected node, and a permission/context-sensitive command bar. These are documented interactions, not runtime observations.
frameforge_implications: Design inference: combine a production graph, node/run inspector, artifact preview, source bin and timeline under the same production context, rather than making the graph replace the video editing workspace.
Design inference: preserve production, selected artifact, node and execution identity across graph/history/preview navigation; display whether the inspector shows draft, published or historical data.
limitations: Native source monitor, video timeline, shot bin and complete video composition were not established; these are FrameForge additions. Documentation does not prove persistent selection, focus restoration, seamless cross-tab state or usability at a particular viewport.

observed_facts: History cloning and JSON copy/import produce reusable copies; database-selected Execute Sub-workflow calls reference another workflow by ID and expose its declared inputs. A child workflow's last-node output returns to the caller, and waiting for child completion is configurable. A reference by workflow ID is not documented as a frozen dependency-version lock.

Exported workflow JSON retains credential names and IDs. This proves credential references can travel with a copied definition; it does not prove independent credentials or automatic channel isolation. Shared workflows can run using credentials not individually shared with the editor; editing nodes bound to unshared credentials is restricted.
Projects group credentials and workflows. Moving removes existing sharing, can optionally share eligible credentials to the target, and warns that missing target credentials may break a workflow.

Current Preview packages, available from 2.27.0, carry workflow nodes, connections, settings, published/archived state, folder/project structure, credential references, table schemas, variables and tags. Credential secrets AND non-secret credential configuration such as host, base URL and region do not travel. Execution/version history, table rows, memberships, sharing, pinned data and static workflow data also do not travel.

Package import defaults to source workflow IDs and new-version conflict resolution; a new-ID option supports independent copies. Credential resolution defaults to ID-only matching among accessible credentials usable by the target project, plus global credentials. Explicit credential bindings override matching with type checks. Missing credentials can become empty placeholders, which block publication.

Package variables match by name using target-project then global scope. Values can travel; existing values default to keep-existing. An overwrite can change a global variable used by other projects without a warning. Copying structural definitions therefore does not imply target-specific configuration is empty or safe.
frameforge_implications: Design inference: define an explicit reuse policy: copy a pinned definition revision, or deliberately call a shared definition. Bind channel/account credentials at the production-instance boundary; do not silently inherit delivery authority from a template.

Design inference: display a before/after target manifest covering credential binding, channel ID, visibility, branding, variables, storage destinations, webhook paths and scheduling. Reset or require confirmation for target-specific settings rather than assuming duplication isolates them.
Design inference: separate reusable branding defaults and exposed parameters from secret bindings and publish permissions. Record source definition ID/revision and destination binding lineage.
limitations: [uncertain] The reviewed official docs do not provide a complete field-by-field guarantee for the editor's Duplicate workflow action, including every credential reference, node-specific destination, webhook identity or setting. Do not turn community/search claims of an exact duplicate into a documented universal guarantee.

Package portability rules are explicitly documented but must not be generalized to every editor copy/paste, JSON import or historical duplicate path. Packages are Preview, not available through editor import/export, and individual options vary by release. Video-channel isolation is a FrameForge requirement, not an intrinsic n8n template concept.

observed_facts: The dated December 2025 v2 announcement separates Save from Publish. Current documentation adds autosave: drafts do not replace the published production graph. Publish makes the selected version live for production webhook/form URLs, schedules and connected-app events. Publishing a workflow is deployment/activation of automation, NOT posting a video to a channel.

Current publishing is asynchronous, with server-persisted Publishing state and documented partial/failed trigger activation outcomes. A published version can exist while no triggers activated, or only some activated. Publishing success must not be assumed from clicking the button. Workflow-settings-only changes are an exception: n8n republishes without a separate explicit publish action, and history says settings do not create a new version.

Enterprise workflow reviews are documented from 2.37.0 as Preview and must be enabled by an instance admin. Reviews pin one saved graph version; later edits do not change that pinned version unless submitted to the review. Approval normally publishes that exact version automatically as the requester, but rare automatic-publish failure can leave an approved closed review requiring manual publication.

An open review blocks publishing through editor, public API and n8n MCP. It does not prevent unpublishing. Review is optional when enabled; the browser-local Review required preference only changes that user's flow and is not a global policy. Reviewers need workflow:read; submit/update needs workflow:publish. Assigned reviewers or project/instance admins can decide.

Review covers nodes and connections, NOT workflow settings, credentials, variables, tables or called sub-workflows. Those changes can affect production immediately even with a review open. A parent graph approval is therefore not approval of all transitive resources or generated media.

The YouTube node separately supports Video Upload, Get and Update operations and requires service credentials. These external operations are distinct from workflow publishing. The n8n node overview does not specify the full current YouTube privacyStatus, OAuth-scope or quota contract.

Package import has explicit publishing policies. Default preserve-published-state leaves new workflows drafts; it only republishes an existing published workflow when the source is published too. Placeholder credentials or unavailable node types block publication. Import can succeed while publication fails, with per-workflow publishing outcomes.
frameforge_implications: Design inference: use distinct actions and statuses for approve artifact, publish workflow definition, authorize external delivery, upload video, set channel visibility and verify remote result.

Design inference: bind media approval to exact output bytes/hash plus production revision and delivery manifest. Invalidate that approval if the artifact or relevant destination/visibility changes, independently of graph review.

Design inference: a final delivery gate should read the resolved destination account/channel, privacy intent, artifact hash, authorization and rights status; then persist the remote video ID and read back actual remote status after upload. Never infer video delivery from workflow execution success or workflow publication.
limitations: [uncertain] No native content-addressed video-artifact approval or automatic invalidation of such approval after edits was established. n8n graph-version review is not evidence of that feature.

No video was uploaded and no permission, quota, OAuth token or privacy setting was inspected. YouTube's current OAuth, privacyStatus and quota contracts require separate official YouTube API research; no defaults or numeric quotas are assumed here. Review and package introduction calendar dates are undated; only minimum versions are documented.

observed_facts: Official shortcuts document arrow-key graph selection, Enter opening the selected node, Escape closing the node panel, node-panel directional category navigation, zoom in/out/reset/fit, and Ctrl/Cmd+K for a contextual permission-sensitive command bar.

Dirty output is documented with an icon as well as a changed border, and a tooltip explaining staleness in the output pane. Publishing documentation describes disabled, ready, published-with-changes, invalid, error, publishing, partial and failure states.

The shortcuts page says Ctrl/Cmd+S saves, whereas the more specific current save/publish page says no manual save is required and maps that shortcut to naming a version. The newer lifecycle documentation is used for save semantics; the conflicting shortcut is not an accessibility guarantee.
frameforge_implications: Design inference: support keyboard graph traversal, explicit focus/selection indicators, a non-color status vocabulary, and textual dirty/error explanations. Keep focus and selected production stable when opening inspectors or history.

Design inference: provide resizable panes and a compact artifact/run view instead of assuming that a full node canvas is usable on narrow screens. Validate screen-reader announcements and keyboard-only completion in the actual FrameForge runtime.
limitations: [uncertain] These sources do not establish WCAG conformance, complete keyboard reachability, screen-reader semantics, focus restoration, mobile usability or responsive breakpoints. No browser or accessibility runtime tests were performed. Documented mouse/touch panning is not proof of a responsive mobile workflow editor.
